name: What is the difference between solid wood and MDF crown molding?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between solid wood and MDF crown molding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wood delivers authentic grain, sharp profiles, and exceptional durability, making it ideal for staining or high-end finish carpentry. However, natural wood contracts and expands with seasonal humidity shifts, making it more prone to seam movement. MDF (medium-density fiberboard) is more affordable, comes pre-primed, and resists temperature-induced warping, but it is strictly for painted finishes and can swell if exposed to water leaks. For rooms where trim will be painted rather than stained, MDF offers a cost-effective, uniform surface that holds paint cleanly across long runs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Solid wood offers natural grain and can be stained or painted, while MDF is a budget-friendly, pre-primed alternative that stays stable during seasonal shifts but is strictly paint-grade.
